text:
alex: Ran an nsys trace on staging after the kernel-selector change — seeing ~12% tail-latency regression on long (2k) sequences. attaching top-level timeline + short nsys command we used.

infra-bot: upload: https://artifacts.redwood/run/2195551111/nsys_trace.qdrep :attached: (job: perf/regression/2195)

alex: command used:
```
nsys profile -o trace_2195 --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=none --stats=true \
  python -m runtime.bench --model=bench-v2 --seq=2048 --batch=4
```

maria: saw the trace. kernel timeline shows repeated small matmul launches interleaved with memcpy and kv-cache path checks. can we annotate each kernel variant better? right now everything is "matmul" and we lose which path (int8 vs fp16, fused-kv vs generic).

sam: agree. we should push nvtx ranges for: request-level, batching-phase, kernel-variant, kv-cache-access. short names only (nvtx label limit kills readability). propose scheme:
- R/<short-hash> (request)
- B/<phase> (batch-assemble|dispatch)
- K/<family>:<variant> (e.g., K/matmul:q4_0)
- C/KV:hit or C/KV:miss

jen: +1 for compact labels. also add a span id on request start so we can correlate many kernels back to the request (don't rely on PID/TID only). something like R/<reqid> with reqid = low-hex(hash(trace_id || seq_start))

dinesh: concern: NVTX push/pop adds overhead when we do per-kernel ranges at hot path. we should gate them behind a runtime flag and a compile-time macro. sampling too large might hide regressions though.

alex: agreed. plan:
- add runtime flag env RUNTIME_TRACE=1 and CMAKE option ENABLE_NVTX_INSTR
- default off in release; enable on canaries and perf runs
- add a short-hash helper to shrink IDs to 8 chars

maria: example C++ helper we can drop into runtime/common/instrument.h:
```
inline std::string span_label(const char *prefix, uint64_t id) {
  char buf[32];
  snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%s/%08x", prefix, (uint32_t)(id & 0xffffffff));
  return std::string(buf);
}

#ifdef ENABLE_NVTX_INSTR
  nvtxRangePushA(span_label("R", req_hash).c_str());
#else
  (void)0;
#endif
```

sam: for kernel-variant labels, use family shortcodes: MM (matmul), GEM (gemm kernel), SCL (scale), MEM (memcpy), PREF (prefetch). example: K/MM:q4_0

jen: we also need KV cache annotations for hit/miss and prefetch vs direct lookup. propose C/KV:H and C/KV:M; include optional small key-hash e.g., C/KV:H:abcd1234

dinesh: sampling plan: run low-overhead enabled for 1% of requests in prod (RUNTIME_TRACE_SAMPLE=0.01) and full traces on staging. that gives signal without heavy perf impact.

alex: actionable items:
- sam: add labeling enum + shortcodes for kernel families (PR)
- maria: add span-id helper + env gating (PR)
- jen: update perf-run docs with nsys command and sampling flags
- dinesh: run a perf matrix comparing with/without nvtx to quantify overhead (small microbench)

infra-bot: created perf ticket INF-4302 and linked artifact https://artifacts.redwood/run/2195551111/nsys_trace.qdrep

maria: one more: when we annotate batching-phase, include batch size and seq-len in the label? that could be K/BATCH:bs4_s2048 — but be careful about label churn. maybe encode parameters in attributes in the trace UI instead of label.

sam: good call. labels for topology, attributes for numeric params.

alex: i'll stitch a perfetto shortlink after the next run. thanks everyone — want the kernel-family mapping before i re-run the long 2k sweep.

jen: I'll update the docs and add a small section on "label hygiene": max 64 chars, avoid spaces, prefer shortcodes + hex ids. also add example grep commands for nvtx ranges in qdrep: `nsys nvtx list trace_2195.qdrep | grep 'K/MM'`

dinesh: FYI I already repro'd the regression locally with the selector change and a 10-run median: tail moved from 28ms -> 31.5ms at seq=2048, batch=4. once labels are in place we can split attribution between kv lookups vs new kernel variant.

sam: cool. i'll start the PR for enums and shortcodes tonight.

alex: perfect. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility :eyes:
